status: Desktop play fits in the window: map on the left, a compact icon rail on the right, explanations in tooltips, and history plus campaign detail closed until opened. Save format unchanged.
request: Offline browser game inspired by Tigers in the Snow on the TRS-80, with similar retro graphics and turn-based gameplay.
scope: Original implementation and scenario, not a reproduction of copyrighted code, artwork, manual, or exact map.
decisions: New campaigns use the player-aid roster, 19 by 11 map, separate movement and combat, and cumulative German VP minus Allied VP. Classic and older Manual saves keep their own rules. Germany needs 8 held points only under those older rules.

The command bar above the map is the selected-formation panel: strength, supply, order guidance, defensive defaults and towns. It had been left hidden, which also disabled opening attacks because the selected id was the old g1 counter.
The map legend names each symbol. The old glyph row read as leftover placeholder text.
German computer orders take an exit only from turn 5 and only after Bastogne, Marche and Rochefort are occupied.
Keep local HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step. ROT.js stays vendored.
validation: Browser play of a new German campaign, an Allied campaign, hotseat, and computer versus computer, including export and import.
knownLimitations: This is an original scenario, not the original game's map or combat tables.
Computer balance is a heuristic. It is not a claim of even wins.
Undo history is session-only and is not part of the save file.
resume: Read this file and the game files before editing. Do not change the save format without a migration. Run the three node test files.
